title: slot-compaction-and-lazy-kernel-probing-notes
content:
Purpose and scope
--
Quick working notes for an alternative approach to handling variable sequence lengths in the serving runtime. Focus is on three related ideas: slot compaction (a lightweight in-batch contraction of token slots), lazy kernel probing (deferred kernel selection based on observed shapes), and KV-aware packing (accounting for KV cache cost when forming batches). This doc collects heuristics, microbench ideas, and rollout constraints.

Why we need something new
--
Current thinking (see related RFCs) has converged on bucketing by seq-length and aggressive prefix padding. That works well for predictable workloads but shows gaps when:
- request length distribution has a long tail with spikes (chat UIs, code completion bursts)
- models with large KV state (long-context LMs) make token cost non-linear — a short addition to a long prefix is expensive because of KV lookups
- multi-tenant Dedicated pools where we want predictable per-tenant latency but also better throughput.

Plain bucketing + static padding leads to:
- wasted GPU cycles when a single long request forces a full-batch padding increase
- suboptimal kernel choices because kernel heuristics assume fixed sequence lengths per batch
- KV cache thrashing when we co-locate requests with distinct prefixes (cache locality matters)

Top-level idea
--
Introduce a runtime layer that:
1) compacts empty or less-used token slots inside an execution batch (slot compaction) to reduce active compute size without rearranging logical ordering exposed to the caller;
2) probes and selects kernels lazily as tokens are materialized during generation (lazy kernel probing) to avoid over-committing to a kernel for an entire batch;
3) uses a KV-aware packing score when assigning requests to batches so we avoid pairing requests with incompatible KV shapes (KV-aware packing).

Design notes: slot compaction
--
What it is: Within a batch we create a logical-to-physical slot map. Physically contiguous slots are compacted to form a smaller shaped tensor for kernel execution. After compute, outputs are scattered back to their logical positions.
Pros:
- Effective reduction in compute for batches with many short sequences or partially-filled attention windows (e.g., when many requests near zero-step continuation)
- Works with existing kernels as long as we can scatter/gather efficiently on device
Cons / risks:
- Scatter/gather overhead might negate benefits if compaction ratio is low (< 1.15x); need microbenchmarks
- Complexity in KV cache indexing: KV idxs must follow logical mapping, adding indirection cost
- Harder to support fused kernels that assume contiguous layout
Implementation sketch:
- Batch builder emits: logical_slot_ids[], desired_seq_len[]
- Runtime computes compaction groups: group contiguous small seqs until GPU memory alignment threshold hit (e.g., 128 token alignment)
- Build compact tensor via device-side gather kernel (fast memcpy-like)
- Run normal attention/FFN kernels on compact tensor
- Scatter results back with device-side scatter kernel
- Maintain a per-batch slot_map: physical_idx -> logical_idx, sent downstream for KV updates
Heuristic parameters (tunable):
- compaction_threshold_ratio (minimum expected speedup to attempt compaction)
- max_scatter_overhead_ms (bail if gather+scatter > X ms)
- alignment_unit (memory layout alignment to satisfy cuBLAS/cuDNN/FlashAttention requirements)

Design notes: lazy kernel probing
--
What it is: Delay final kernel selection until right before execution or even mid-generation when partial shapes are known. We maintain a small portfolio of compatible kernels (quantized, fused, non-fused) and pick based on: sequence length distribution in physical tensor, presence of KV, memory pressure, and current throughput SLO.
Why useful:
- Avoids choosing a heavy low-latency kernel for a batch that will shrink quickly in subsequent steps
- Allows switching to differently-optimized kernels mid-rollout for the same logical batch (requires careful pinning of memory layouts)
Mechanism:
- Batch metadata carries a kernel_candidate_list prioritized by expected cost.
- Just-in-time probe: run a tiny micro-kernel (profiling run) on a small sample of the batch (e.g., first 8 rows) to estimate real throughput of each candidate on current device temp/queue load. Probing cost must be bounded (e.g., <= 0.5 ms).
- If best candidate differs from default, switch and run full batch. For generation, allow probe every N steps or when compaction triggers change.
Tradeoffs:
- Extra complexity in memory manager and kernel registry
- Probing increases scheduling jitter; we must not violate tail latency SLOs
- Need fallback to deterministic kernel if probing results inconsistent

Design notes: KV-aware packing
--
Observation: Two requests with similar current generation lengths can still be expensive together if their KV shapes diverge (e.g., one has long prefix and rich KV while the other has minimal KV). We should include KV shape into packing score.
Packing score components (simple additive model):
- seq_len_score = normalized(seq_len)
- kv_size_score = normalized(kv_memory_bytes) * kv_penalty_factor
- prefix_similarity_bonus = n_common_prefix_tokens / max_prefix_limit (encourages co-location of similar prefixes for KV reuse)
- latency_sla_penalty: requests with tight SLA get negative score so we prioritize low-latency placement
Implementation notes:
- Collect kv_memory_bytes estimate from KV store compact metadata (we already maintain approximate per-request KV size)
- Prefix similarity computed via hashed prefix fingerprint (first N tokens hashed into 64-bit), matching fingerprints give bonus
- Packing uses greedy first-fit decreasing with these composite scores; keep O(n log n) scaling per batch builder

Microbench plan (short list)
--
1) Device scatter/gather micro (CUDA): measure gather + kernel + scatter overhead on A100 and H100 for compaction ratios 1.05..2.0. Vary row lengths and alignment units.
2) Probing overhead: implement a probe harness that runs 3 candidate kernels on first 8 rows and returns a ranked list. Measure overhead distribution on cold vs warmed GPUs.
3) KV-aware packing simulation: replay production traces (1 week sample) with offline packing simulator to measure throughput and tail latency changes. Include metrics: tokens/sec, GPU occupancy, repacked KV misses, KV locality (hit rate).
4) End-to-end A/B: enable compaction+probing for 10% of traffic on dedicated pool with monitoring for 95/99th latency and cost-per-token.

Compatibility notes and constraints
--
- Must remain compatible with existing API (no changes to client-visible ordering or token ids). Compaction is purely an internal physical mapping layer.
- For private/on-prem deployments we need a toggle; default off for initial rollout. Document a knob: runtime.enable_slot_compaction and runtime.lazy_kernel_probing with safety limits.
- Observability: per-batch telemetry must include: compaction_ratio, probe_choice, probe_latency_ms, pre/post KV memory footprint, slot_map checksum. Add labels to traces to let Console show when compaction occurred.

Open questions / risks
--
- What is the right granularity: per-batch only or per-operator (attention vs FFN)? Could compaction be applied to attention but not to matmuls?
- Scatter/gather kernel design: should be fused with attention kernel to eliminate copy? Fusing reduces portability and increases kernel maintenance.
- Memory pinning: compaction increases memory fragmentation; need allocator adjustments.
- Interaction with multi-device sharding (tensor parallel): compaction could upset alignment of shards across devices. Need cross-device slot_map coordination.
- Security: ensure compaction mapping doesn't accidentally leak across tenants when using shared device memory (should be fine but audit).

Action items / next steps
--
- (Maya) write CUDA microbench for gather/scatter and iterate with infra; target: first results by 2024-03-08.
- (Arjun) prototype probe harness inside runtime kernel registry; include 3 candidate kernels (flash-attn, non-fused, quantized-fused) — PR draft by 2024-03-15.
- (Sofia) run offline KV-aware packing simulation on 7-day production sample; share dashboard snapshots by 2024-03-12.
- (Eliot) investigate allocator changes required for compaction and cross-device pointer mapping; report risks by 2024-03-10.

Notes to reviewers
--
- This is a sketchy, intentionally exploratory doc. Looking for feedback on:
  - whether compaction is a plausible win vs smarter packing & prefix clustering (trade CPU vs GPU work)
  - heuristics for probing frequency and probe budget
  - interaction with TP/DP sharding and Dedicated pool fairness policies

References and existing work to compare:
--
- prior: "prefix-clustering-kv-routing-and-padding-strategy" (see drive) — similar goal but different approach (pre-batch clustering vs this run-time compaction)
- prior: late-binding-kernel-selection notes — overlaps on kernel selection but here probing is explicitly micro-run based
- internal perf tests: infra/perf/flash-attn-bench-2023 (linked in the PR above)

Random brainstorms (parking lot)
--
- Can we make compaction incremental: keep a hot workspace where short sequences are pre-compacted and reused across batches? Would save gather cost but complicate correctness.
- Use hardware memcpy engines (DMA) for gather/scatter to minimize kernel overhead if supported.
- Explore a probabilistic packing: accept occasional small wasted tokens to avoid scatter entirely for ultra-low-latency lanes.
